stories.title: How can we explain psychosomatic illnesses?
stories.summary: Emotions play a significant part in physical symptoms – but not in the way people often imagine When Diego started seeing bright flashing lights in his field of vision and felt his legs go weak, he thought he knew immediately what was happening. His mother had a stroke in her 60s, and although Diego was active and (unlike his mother) didn’t smoke, he had always expected that the same would happen to him. So it was a huge relief to be told – after seeing a stroke specialist and having a brain scan – that he had not had a stroke at all. Unfortunately the relief was short-lived. The visual disturbances and the weakness were real and debilitating. If this wasn’t a stroke, what was it? Some illnesses aren’t caused by disease or damage, but arise when the coordinated functioning of the body goes awry. In a percentage of these cases a person’s psychological health is an important element in their symptoms. Intuitively this seems mysterious. We are accustomed to thinking about physical symptoms as being caused by physical events; viruses, inflammation, bleeding. How can something as intangible as a thought have any impact on something as physical as a leg? How can the mind make us ill? Continue reading...

stories.title: They went out to celebrate at a Memphis bar. Then, ICE descended
stories.summary: More than 120 people in the Tennessee city were detained in one of the largest single-day ICE raids in the US in 2026 The date 1 September, or 9/01 Day, is a festive day for Memphians. The date mirrors the city’s 901 area code, and gives residents a reason to come together to celebrate the city and the people who love it. When 9/01 Day falls on a weekday, as it did this year, the celebration starts the weekend prior, extending the festivities. Groups across the city hosted celebrations featuring food vendors, DJs, musicians and members of the Memphis Grizzlies , the local NBA team, while dozens of local businesses offered $9.01-themed specials. But for the families of 121 people, this past 1 September will be remembered for a different reason – just days prior, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained their friends and relatives, conducting one of the largest single-day raids in the country this year, and the largest known one in Memphis . stories.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
stories.summary: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube , ai , generative-ai , llms , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai-misuse
